summary: H.R. 4183, the Federal Maritime Commission Reauthorization Act of 2025, reauthorizes the Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 with funding levels of $49,200,000 per year. The legislation expands the FMC's regulatory and investigative authority over international ocean transportation, broadens oversight of controlled carriers tied to nonmarket or monitored economies, requires the agency to investigate complaints against shipping exchanges, establishes new national advisory committees, and places restrictions on the public disclosure of enforcement investigation documents.

affected_groups.effect: Receives reauthorization and funding, expanded regulatory authority over international shipping, new reporting duties, and restrictions on disclosing investigative documents.
Carriers linked legally or financially to nonmarket economy countries or nations monitored by the U.S. Trade Representative face expanded regulatory oversight.
Subject to mandatory FMC investigation of complaints regarding market manipulation or anticompetitive practices, and new rulemakings on freight price indexes.
Represented on the newly established National Port Advisory Committee to advise the FMC on freight delivery system policies.
affected_groups.group: Marine Terminal Operators, Port Authorities, and Maritime Labor

key_provisions: Authorizes appropriations for the Federal Maritime Commission of $49,200,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
Expands the definition of controlled carriers subject to extra oversight to include carriers linked to nonmarket economies or countries monitored by the U.S. Trade Representative.
Requires the FMC to accept and investigate information and complaints regarding market manipulation or anticompetitive practices by registered shipping exchanges.
Establishes a National Port Advisory Committee and a National Ocean Carrier Advisory Committee to advise the FMC alongside the existing Shipper Committee.
Prohibits the disclosure of FMC investigation documents unless the commission determines by majority vote they are relevant to a proceeding and votes to release them.
Mandates new annual reporting requirements, including analyses of trade imbalances and aggregated findings from the Vessel-Operating Common Carrier Audit Program.
Directs the FMC to issue an advance notice of proposed rulemaking within one year and a final rule within three years regarding containerized freight price indexes.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 4183, the Federal Maritime Commission Reauthorization Act of 2025, reauthorizes the Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 with funding levels of $49,200,000 per year. The legislation expands the FMC's regulatory and investigative authority over international ocean transportation, broadens oversight of controlled carriers tied to nonmarket or monitored economies, requires the agency to investigate complaints against shipping exchanges, establishes new national advisory committees, and places restrictions on the public disclosure of enforcement investigation documents.
summary_detail.significance: The bill updates the funding, oversight powers, and advisory structure of the Federal Maritime Commission, impacting international ocean shipping regulations, trade monitoring, and federal investigations into foreign trade practices and shipping exchanges.
